text:
marta: quick heads-up — onboarding sample (go-starter) shows early logs with request_id=undefined when OTEL_LOG_INJECTION=true. also seeing duplicated [REDACTED] fragments making logs noisy.

chen: thanks. raw example?

marta: `2026-06-18T09:12:03Z INFO http.request path=/chat request_id=undefined user_email=[REDACTED] duration=18ms` then later `request_id=ry7c...`

oscar: sounds like reqid middleware not initialized before first log. we should never emit literal "undefined" — default to `-` or `init` and guard casts.

chen: double-redact could be our redactor + OTEL exporter's redaction both running. if our regex matches the placeholder it can create noisy repeated tokens like `[REDACTED]-[REDACTED]`.

marta: proposal: (1) change reqid lookup to `rid, _ := ctx.Value(reqIDKey).(string); if rid=="" { rid="init" }` (2) make redaction idempotent: skip if value already contains `[REDACTED]`.

oscar: add unit tests: simulate OTEL injecting trace id after logger and simulate two redaction passes. also add a small CI smoke test in examples/ci that starts sample with OTEL_LOG_INJECTION=true and fails if `request_id=undefined` or duplicate `[REDACTED]` tokens found.

marta: i'll open a tiny PR with the defensive cast and redactor early-out + repro script. will link issues.

synth-bot: NOTE: created issue #4532 (devex) "go-starter: early request_id undefined + non-idempotent redactor" by marta

chen: great. one more thought — prefer merging fields rather than overwriting when OTEL later injects data, to avoid losing fields.

oscar: agreed. add test for merge semantics.

marta: PR up in 15m, ping here for reviews. thanks!
